'''Svatopluk Poljak''' (also known as '''Sváťa Poljak'''; 9 October 1951 – 2 April 1995) was a Czech mathematician known for his work in [[discrete mathematics]] and [[combinatorial optimization]].

== Biography ==
Poljak was born in [[Prague]], [[Czechoslovakia]] (now the [[Czech Republic]]). In 1980, he earned his PhD in mathematics from [[Charles University]] in Prague under the supervision of [[Zdeněk Hedrlín]] and [[Jaroslav Nešetřil]].<ref>{{MathGenealogy |id=100178}}</ref> Upon completing his PhD, he took a position at the [[Czech Technical University in Prague]] in the Department of Operations Research, and in 1986, he returned to Charles University for a senior research position in the Department of Applied Mathematics. While at Charles University, he was invited for extended academic visits to Kyoto, New Brunswick, Paris, Bonn and Taipei. He was awarded a [[Alexander von Humboldt Foundation|Humboldt Fellowship]] for his 18-month stay in Bonn.<ref name="uni-passau">{{cite web |title=Poljak Lecture |url=https://www.fim.uni-passau.de/en/discrete-mathematics/poljak-lecture |website=University of Passau |access-date=27 June 2025}}</ref> In 1994, he became a professor of mathematics at the [[University of Passau]].

On 2 April 1995, Poljak died in a car accident travelling from his summer house in the village of [[Nové Hutě]] to Prague.<ref name="In memory of Svatopluk Poljak">{{cite journal |title=In memory of Svatopluk Poljak |journal=Mathematical Programming |date=April 1997 |volume=77 |issue=1 |pages=97–104 |doi=10.1007/BF02614430}}</ref>

== Contributions ==
Poljak made many important contributions in diverse areas of discrete mathematics, including [[matroid|matroid theory]], [[matching (graph theory)|matching theory]], the [[maximum cut|max-cut]] and [[independent set (graph theory)|stable set]] problems, [[spectral graph theory]], convex and polyhedral relaxations, [[semidefinite programming]], and other [[integer programming]]-related problems. His early work also included contributions to the theory of [[neural network (machine learning)|neural networks]].<ref name="In memory of Svatopluk Poljak" /> Over the course of his career, Poljak authored over 90 scientific papers. His frequent coauthors include Daniel Turzík, [[Vojtěch Rödl]], Martin Loebl, [[Monique Laurent]], Franz Rendl, [[Jaroslav Nešetřil]], {{ill|Zsolt Tuza|hu|Tuza Zsolt}}, and Aleš Pultr.<ref>{{cite web |title=Svatopluk Poljak |url=https://mathscinet.ams.org/mathscinet/author?authorId=192349 |website=MathSciNet |publisher=American Mathematical Society |access-date=27 June 2025}}</ref>

== Recognition ==
The book ''Handbook of Semidefinite Programming: Theory, Algorithms, and Applications'', published in 2000, was dedicated to the memory of Svatopluk Poljak.<ref name="Handbook of semidefinite programming">{{cite book |title=Handbook of Semidefinite Programming: Theory, Algorithms, and Applications |date=2000 |publisher=Springer Science+Business Media |location=New York, New York |isbn=978-1-4613-6970-7 |editor-last1=Wolkowicz |editor-first1=Henry |editor-last2=Saigal |editor-first2=Romesh |editor-last3=Vandenberghe |editor-first3=Lieven}}</ref> In 2025, an annual lecture series, entitled the "Poljak Lecture", was established in honour of Poljak at the [[University of Passau]].<ref name="uni-passau"/>
